result.title: Thinking Fast, Trading Late: System One Decision Models vs the Market
result.comment: 40 pages, 12 figures, 12 tables; pre-registered (analysis plan frozen by hash before the test period was unblinded); code at https://github.com/AmirDehkordi/NewsAction
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) read company news at scale, and backtests suggest that their readings predict stock returns. We ask how much of that predictability survives a test that rules out look-ahead, memorization and selection. We propose OLIVIA, a protocol for such tests: point-in-time inputs with company identities masked, selection on validation data only, an analysis plan frozen by cryptographic hash, and a test period unblinded once through a logged lock. We apply it to AI decision models, non-generative language models that return probabilities for typed questions, reading news about S&P 500 stocks: an open-weights model we fine-tuned on 2024-2025 data, three commercial models and standard baselines. The fine-tuned model's signal replicated on two validation quarters (daily information coefficients 0.055 and 0.065) but fell to 0.020 (t = 1.7) on the blinded January-July 2026 test. The commercial models' readings line up with the overnight move to the open (information coefficient 0.074 to 0.077) but not with the move after it, so the news is priced by the time a trader can act on it at the open. No model can tell over- from under-reaction, and no pre-registered strategy survives costs and a deflated Sharpe ratio. Commercial models identify masked companies in 62% to 74% of cases against a 28% baseline: masking hides names, not companies. The market reads the news first.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 OLIVIA 预注册评测协议——时点化输入、公司身份掩码、仅用验证集选型、哈希冻结分析计划、单次解盲测试期，并用它检验 LLM 类决策模型读新闻对美股收益的预测力，发现信号在解盲期大幅衰减，且掩码并不能隐藏公司身份。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是排除前视、记忆与选择偏差的严格评测设计，可供核查 LVR 中「latent 内容是否真正因果参与决策」的验证方式，掩码后仍被识别也提示捷径泄漏风险；但该文不涉及多模态推理状态，联系仅在评价方法层面。
